headline: High: shared MCP and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks; OpenBB’s finance data amplifies compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and OpenBBTerminal also exposes MCP servers, so a shared bridge exists. Haystack’s broad network egress and OpenBB’s “connect once, consume everywhere” pattern make it plausible that one agent’s outputs are consumed by the other without provenance checks. The pairwise pathway is documented only at the profile level, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are connected to the same MCP server or broker, injection becomes reachable.
IF OpenBB consumes Haystack-produced text as instructions, prompt hijack risk increases.
mitigations: Disable shared MCP endpoints between the agents.
Require provenance tags on all inter-agent messages.
Route Haystack output through a strict JSON schema.
Add a human review step before OpenBB acts on Haystack text.
requires-engineering: implement allowlisted tool-call parsing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and OpenBBTerminal handles financial, licensed, and public data. If they share an MCP or workspace bridge, Haystack can transmit OpenBB-derived sensitive context outward, while OpenBB may ingest Haystack outputs into its own backend flows. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange data through a shared MCP server, leakage becomes plausible.
IF OpenBB processes financial or licensed data in the same session as Haystack, sensitive context can cross boundaries.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Block Haystack egress to non-approved destinations.
Do not pass financial or licensed data into Haystack prompts.
Use redaction before any inter-agent handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent network and data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and MCP access, while OpenBBTerminal has MCP access but no filesystem write, shell, or git modification. That limits direct write-write conflict. The main overlap is shared tool access rather than competing mutable state, so the blast radius is small unless an external orchestrator grants both write authority.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource, conflict risk rises.
IF both agents are pointed at the same MCP tool with side effects, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate tool credentials per agent.
Avoid shared mutable resources.
Serialize any side-effecting tool calls.
Monitor for conflicting writes in the orchestrator.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG system, so its outputs are likely to be treated as retrieved facts, and OpenBBTerminal is a financial-modeling agent that can act on those inputs. If OpenBB consumes Haystack output without verification, a mistaken retrieval can cascade into incorrect financial analysis or downstream actions. The profiles suggest the pathway, but not a documented verification step.
conditions: IF OpenBB uses Haystack output as authoritative input, cascading error is reachable.
IF Haystack retrieves stale or incorrect facts, OpenBB may propagate them into reports or actions.
mitigations: Require source citations on Haystack outputs.
Have OpenBB re-check critical facts against primary sources.
Insert a confidence threshold before acting on retrieved data.
Log and review any high-impact downstream decisions.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBB touches financial and licensed data, while Haystack has broad network egress and MCP access. If regulated financial or licensed data flows from OpenBB into Haystack, Haystack’s external connectivity can create a compliance breach or residency/retention mismatch. The profiles do not show HIPAA, but they do show sensitive financial data and outbound-capable infrastructure, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is routed from OpenBB into Haystack, compliance exposure is present.
IF retention or logging policies differ between the two agents, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Haystack prompts.
Restrict Haystack to anonymized inputs only.
Review logging and retention settings on both agents.
Document a data-flow boundary for financial data.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
